national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) — portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration single portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (operated by INPI); customs and export data interface: douane.gouv.fr (DELTA/DX)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in France that carries out a taxable French economic activity must file Form No. 13967*01 (EU/EEA/UK resident) or Form No. 13968*01 (non-EU resident) with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). The filing must include apostilled constitutional documents of the foreign entity, certified French translations, proof of address or appointment of a French fiscal representative, and a statement of intended activities. DGFIP then issues a SIREN/SIRET number for any permanent establishment or direct taxable nexus and, if VAT-liable transactions are present, a French VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire, format FR+key+SIREN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the entity level under Articles 206 et seq. CGI, irrespective of the ISIC 7310 service activity; the territorial principle limits French taxation to French-source profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime; classification follows the CGI legal form. Available elections: (i) option for income-tax treatment under Article 239 bis A CGI for qualifying small SARLs; (ii) option for VAT grouping as a single taxable person (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C bis CGI; (iii) election for French fiscal integration under Article 223 A CGI for 95%-owned subsidiaries; (iv) hybrid-mismatch neutralization elections under Articles 212 bis et seq. CGI transposing ATAD 2 (payee/granting jurisdiction additional-tax disallowance elections).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA under Article 293 B CGI: €36,800 annual turnover for service activities (€91,900 for goods activities); however, non-established suppliers making taxable supplies in France are mandatorily registrable without any threshold, and cross-border B2C electronic services may be declared via the OSS/IOSS regime. For a French SARL engaged in ISIC 7310 advertising/ASO services, registration is mandatory upon exceeding the €36,800 service threshold, and B2B services to French VAT-registered clients are reverse-charged.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing reform: all B2B and B2C transactions must be transmitted via a DGFIP-registered PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) with simultaneous e-reporting of transaction data; B2G e-invoicing via Chorus Pro is already mandatory. Large and mid-size companies must comply by 1 September 2026, SMEs and micro-enterprises by 1 September 2027. No fiscal stamping/pre-clearance model applies; instead, immutable structured Factur-X/INVOIC syntax is transmitted in near-real time through certified APIs, with full audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (i) exports of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU with proof of export (Article 262 I 6° CGI); (ii) services the place of supply of which is outside France, notably B2B services supplied to a non-EU established recipient under Article 259-1 CGI and B2C digital/intangible services supplied to non-EU consumers under Article 259 D CGI. SEO, ASO and localization services fall under the general B2B place-of-supply rule; when the customer is established outside the EU the supply is outside the scope of French VAT, with input VAT recovery strictly limited to French taxable activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation via DELTA/DX under the Union Customs Code, with MRN and exit summary)
Transport document (Bill of Lading or Air Waybill) evidencing physical departure from France/EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment evidence (FRX attestation) demonstrating receipt of export proceeds within the statutory period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP may reassess VAT within the 6-year statutory period (10 years in cases of fraud/occult activity) and apply penalties of up to 80% for gross negligence or fraudulent zero-rating claims under Articles 1728, 1729 and 1731 CGI, plus delay interest of 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI. Fabricated export documentation engages criminal customs liability under Article 414 Code des douanes, including confiscation and fines up to twice the value of the goods, and automatic denial of VAT refund claims for fictitious exports. Claims are cross-matched against the customs ECS liquidation system and DELTA export records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, Directorate General of Foreign Trade (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; the Eurosystem (European Central Bank) for monetary policy and the ECB regulation on statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full euro convertibility for current account transactions, including cross-border service charges and profit remittances, subject to standard transaction documentation. Capital account transactions are also freely convertible within the EU, while non-EU direct investments require post-transaction statistical declaration to Banque de France (DSI/DRP forms) when amounts exceed €15,000. Profit remittances by a SARL are treated as current account payments and require only a valid corporate resolution and normal accounting documentation. There is no prior exchange control authorization for genuine commercial or investment flows. For non-EU resident shareholders, dividend distribution is subject to the parent–subsidiary directive (if eligible at 5% or more shareholding) or the applicable double tax treaty; the remittance itself faces no convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the state in France. All export receipts may be retained in a domestic or foreign foreign-currency account. For statistical balance of payments reporting, cross-border receipts exceeding €15,000 (or the lower €1,500 if reporting to Banque de France per general regulation on monetary and financial code provisions) must be reported by the bank on behalf of the company on a monthly basis through the 'Entreprises' reporting channel (BOF-SAIP). Companies are not required to convert export proceeds into euros, but for operational liquidity and hedge accounting a natural conversion may be performed. The standard statutory timeline for declaring the transaction to Banque de France is within one working day of the transaction for the reporting bank, with the company having no direct filing obligation but providing supporting documents upon request. Any non-EU invoicing above €12,500 or cumulative €125,000 requires an invoice-related movement declaration field and can be handled electronically by the bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for inbound fee collection and low-value trade settlement, but subject to important legal constraints. Wise (TransferWise Ltd, EMI licensed in Belgium and passported to France) can be opened remotely with a French SIREN, proof of identity, and UBO declaration; it provides a French IBAN (FR76) and EU SEPA direct debit capabilities. Payoneer (Payoneer Europe Ltd, EMI in Ireland) strongly supports marketplaces and freelance B2B receipts in multiple currencies, with onshore USD balances and settlement to the French SARL operating account. Qonto and Shine (backed by Société Générale) are fully licensed as payment institutions (or agents) and act as regulated EMIs registered with the ACPR; they provide domestic and cross-border SEPA payments without a full banking license. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI cannot extend credit, overdraft, or foreign exchange forwards without a credit institution licence, so forward hedging must be provided by a bank or registered broker; (ii) trust-account balances may not be protected by the French deposit guarantee (FGDR), only by safeguarding requirements under the E-Money Directive; (iii) for premiums above €10,000 per month, the entity should supplement EMI rails with a bank account to maintain corporate treasury stability and audit alignment. The recommendation is a 'hybrid' setup: primary Tier-1 bank for FX and clearing, plus Wise/Payoneer for low-cost disbursement and local unattached market fees. An offshore EMI not registered in France (e.g., a non-EU payment provider) is not permitted to hold a French corporate account and may not provide a local IBAN; such an entity would only be a receivable settlement tool using payout to bank accounts, and under PSD2 requires the DevOps agent to verify AML compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In France, the physical presence of a director is not an absolute statutory requirement. However, for first-time corporate accounts, most major French banks require at least one gerant/director to appear in person for a 'calage' interview or to complete a remoted video-verification via a notarized identity check (authentification électronique). Law PACTE and the 2016 AML decree allow remote onboarding if the bank uses a recognised video identity verification service (Ariat Group, IDnow, or bank's DETECT tool). The recommended defence is to prepare a compliance pack (KYC with statutory audits, UBO registry extract) and to allow the chairperson to attend a meeting with the local branch agent if the account volume exceeds €50,000/year or if the beneficial owner is non-EU. In practice, a remote online process is available at BNP Paribas, Societe Generale (via Hello bank!), Qonto, and Wise, but at the final account activation stage a French-registered company must present an official 'Kbis' (extract from the Commercial Registry) dated within three months. If the entity is not yet incorporated, a provisional account ('compte en formation') can be opened by the shareholder with a minimum deposit, though the Kbis must be submitted within 60 days. A power of attorney (Mandat) is accepted for secondary signatories only; the gérant (non-EU director) may not entirely avoid biometric verification. The onboarding timeline ranges 5–15 business days for an online EMI, 15–30 days for a traditional bank with a French branch, and 3–6 weeks for a fully remote multinational with enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign (non-French) ownership of the SARL, especially when ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is resident outside the EEA or in a high-risk third country (as defined by the FATF list).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of passport; a company excerpt from the Registry of Commerce (extrait Kbis); a legalised certificate from a local notary or embassy confirming identity; a signed UBO declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs) submitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; audited or notarised funding source evidence (bank reference letter from the foreign branch, salary slips, tax returns or cryptocurrency-related provenance letter if relevant); and a business plan articulating the app growth agency's revenue model, client contracts, and forecast cash flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity and cross-border third-party settlement flows (e.g., receiving fees from app stores, foreign publishers, and paying subcontractors worldwide) that resemble payment intermediation or money service business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a drafted service agreement with each major counterparty and an AML self-assessment report showing that the Taiwan company does not collect, hold or transfer external money on behalf of third parties, and that each transaction is pre-approved by the client with clear commercial purpose. Present a detailed KYC file of the top 10 counterparties (legal name, registered address, tax ID) and an outline of the company's internal sanctions screening process using a reputable provider (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check) to demonstrate that no PEP/high-risk jurisdiction relationships are activated without enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid deposit surges or immediate outbound payments (layering pattern) from a newly opened corporate account within the first 90 days, especially when combined with invoices to tax havens or jurisdictions not aligned with FATF standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a treasury historical ledger (monthly) with the invoice reference, bank purpose code, corresponding proof of contract, and a description of the good/service (e.g., App Store Optimization, ASO, SEO, mobile advertising) for each transaction. Provide a board resolution authorising the payment pattern; prior bank statements from the company's previous banking relationship showing the same business activity; and a letter from the company's registered accountant (Expert-Comptable) confirming that the flows are consistent with the SARL's declared revenue and tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear origin of funds when subscribing to capital, particularly if the shareholder contributes euros converted from a foreign currency in amounts greater than €15,000.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a transfer certificate from your outgoing bank showing the source account, a signed declaration on honour (attestation) of the shareholder stating that the funds come from accumulated savings, dividends, salary, or sale of previous business; a copy of the notarised deed of incorporation with the share subscription evidence; and a receipt from the French account institution for the deposit confirming the SWIFT code and reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repeated disbursements to offshore advertising platforms or to digital asset exchanges (for billing/invoicing purposes) that may be viewed as round-tripping to evade tax or capital controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain an export/import invoice with a clear purchase order; keep a complete file of the supply agreement with the ad network (e.g., Meta, Google, TikTok) or media buying platform; a breakdown of user acquisition costs by campaign and period; an independent audit conducted by a French certified accountant confirming that the transactions are at arm's length and correspond to the actual performance marketing services rendered.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection for the French SARL may be made via international wire transfer using SWIFT MT103 (for EUR credit to a French IBAN) or SEPA InST for EU-origin transactions. The reference field must contain the ISIN of the company (SIREN/SIRET) and the purpose code 'D5 – Direct investment in the capital of a French company' or 'O1 – Other investment' depending on the non-resident ownership structure. For non-resident owner injection above €15,000, the shareholder must complete and provide to the bank a 'Declaration Cerfa 15555*01' (participation in the financing of a French company) within 20 business days of the payment. The bank will automatically file the 'Déclaration Statistique et Financière' with the Banque de France using the following standard BOP code: 'BF3102 – Foreign investment in the creation or expansion of a commercial enterprise'. A copy of the corporate resolution (PV d'AG) increasing the share capital must be provided. If the capital is paid into a provisional account before registration, the funds must be blocked until the Kbis is issued; after the Kbis, the bank reclassifies the funds as paid-up capital. The routing must be the France-Based bank's SWIFT BIC: e.g., BNPAFRPP, SOGE FRPP, CRLYFRPP (Crédit Agricole). For hedge accounting, foreign currency excess cash should be repatriated at month-end to avoid uncovered positional FX risk; for daily liquidity above EUR 50,000, use a money market sweep or overnight deposit line (DAV, Genie) at the main bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail to Luxembourg or non-EU counterparties is the SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer, with the mandatory purpose code 'Service charges' (code 22) for consultancy/marketing fees. For payments inside the EU below €100,000, SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) are permissible and cheapest; however for cross-border non-EU disbursements above USD limits, MT103 should be used via the bank's international gateway. Documentary instruments include Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) and at-sight documentary collection, although given the SME service business, a bank transfer with proforma invoice is customary. For payments to subcontractors via Wise Business, the rail is an EEA internal transfer to Wise's European IBAN (e.g., BG24... for France), from which Wise executes an Agent's MT103 in local currency. For FX conversions for trade settlement, the bank provides treasury execution via a spot transaction (T+2) and can support same-day value with a 'S.T.P. FX' service. The recommended clearing structure: (i) all non-EUR fees are collected in original currency by a multi-currency sweep account (EUR/GBP/USD), (ii) conversion is done via bank forward or FX Forward contract for the top 70% of forecast receivables, (iii) euro payments issued via SEPA for EU counterparts, and MT103 for non-EU service providers. Invoices must include a VAT clause if billed to French clients, and for B2B cross-border services allow the reverse-charge mechanism. All outbound instructions require the beneficiary's IBAN (if shudder) or SWIFT/ABA code coupled with a mandatory 14-digit reference matching the trade invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign Exchange Forward (Outright EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with tenors from 1 week to 12 months, requiring underlying commercial receivable/payable exposure and an executed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the French bank's standard treasury terms.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for currencies without free convertibility (e.g., Egyptian pound, Argentine peso, Nigerian naira, offshore RMB) but strictly forbidden with all EU residents under Regulation (EC) 974/98 without the trade being for a documented export/import exposure; in practice, French 'crédit documentaire' banks allow NDFs for hedging EMEA trade flows only through an authorized broker.

Currency Swaps (FX Swap) for converting temporary surplus EUR into foreign currency for a specified period, with an agreement to reverse at spot or forward at maturity; allows the company to fund local branch payroll or market-specific ad campaigns without using a deposit.

European-Style EUR/USD Options (call/put) through an OTC dealer (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale) for hedging budgeted transactional exposure, requiring a credit line approval by the bank's global markets desk.

SEPA Forex Contracts via Fintech API (e.g., Ebury, Wise Embedded) which are bilateral over-the-counter contracts not exchange-traded, permissible under Marcy in France if the intermediary is registered with the ACPR or an exempted authorised foreign entity under the European passport, and only used to mitigate commercial FX risk, not for speculation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of shareholding and legal particulars (Confirmation Annuelle de l'Identité des Associés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the annual ordinary general assembly approving accounts, and no later than six months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 3,000 per instance (individual) or EUR 15,000 (legal entity); prolonged non-compliance can trigger judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the general assembly, and no later than seven months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 3,000 (individual) or EUR 15,000 (legal entity); fines per article L.232-23 Commercial Code, plus potential Court order to file; persistent failure leads to strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Déclaration de Résultat, Cerfa 2065 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via online filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 3 for previous fiscal year-end between December 31 and January 1 (electronic filing); for other year-ends, within three months of fiscal year closing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due, increasing 0.5% per month for fraud/failure; 40% penalty for deliberate omission; 80% for fraudulent abuse

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual real estate tax return (Déclaration de taxe foncière, if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally May 15 for properties existing as of January 1; note non-resident digital agencies rarely own real property.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Notification of tax reassessment plus late-payment interest and penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise/social solidarity tax on incorporated companies (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by December 15 for the current year, based on prior-year conditions; due by December 15.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late filing penalty; late payment interest; administrative levies; potential suspension of public procurement eligibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return of beneficial owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed initially at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change; no separate annual filing unless changes occur.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning to comply; possible insolvency proceedings; criminal fine up to EUR 30,000 for legal entity, plus imprisonment for directors in case of fraud

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (Commissaire aux Comptes) if any two of three thresholds exceeded at fiscal year-end: (a) total balance sheet exceeding EUR 4,000,000, (b) net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000, (c) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Below thresholds, audit may be voluntarily appointed or required by shareholders/testament. Small SARL exemptions apply for micro-entities under 7a L.612-4 Commercial Code.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2016-06) aligned with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS mandatory for consolidated public-interest entities but optional for individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing in France; any change in direct or indirect ownership, or control, must be declared within 30 days through the Guichet Unique. The RCS record is deemed accurate and non-updated may be deemed a criminal offence. Annual shareholder confirmation intended for updating the RCS registry occurs during the annual general meeting approving accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Decisions (Décisions de l'Associé Unique or Procès-Verbaux d'Assemblées)
Register of Pledges and Securities (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,600 – USD 6,500 per year (EUR 2,300 – EUR 5,800) for a small-to-mid French SARL with no audit mandate; lower if voluntary review is used; higher if mandatory audit applies

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) filed electronically at impots.gouv.fr / EFI teleprocedure; ancillary schedules 2050-2059 plus special forms (e.g., 2065-SD) may be attached.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayment installments (acomptes) of IS are due March, June, September, and December (or in month following first day of fiscal year for non-calendar year).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year-end SARL: May 3 of the following year; for other fiscal year endings: within 3 months of the balance sheet date, extended to the 3rd day of the following month where applicable. Online filing is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity: legal form (SARL), SIREN, APE code (7310Z), registered address, non-resident shareholder details if any, election of director status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French SARL fully owned by non-residents, the field states the French registered office and appoints the gérant; the foreign parent is not itself the taxpayer. Non-resident shareholders need not appear unless they are gérant and are receiving remuneration reported elsewhere.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit/loss before corporate tax, after French GAAP accruals and adjustments to statutory reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL's accounting result must reflect all French activity income, including ASO/SEO localization fees billed to EU and non-EU clients; non-resident owners cannot attribute income to the foreign entity merely because payment rails are held abroad (Wise/Payoneer).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior years available to reduce taxable income after statutory cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deficits realized by the French SARL and computed under French rules may be carried forward; non-resident parent losses are not transferable. The annual cap applies: €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above €1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after reintegration of non-deductible charges, deduction of prior deficits, and application of reduced rate if eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate at 25% standard rate; 15% reduced rate may apply to first €42,500 profit only for small SARLs meeting turnover/capital conditions. Non-resident shareholders cannot benefit from individual exemptions of the French entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Rémunérations de gérant et honoraires versés à des entités étrangères
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct management remuneration and fees paid to related foreign entities (e.g., parent for marketing or tech support).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Such cross-border service fees must be arm's length; if paid to a related person abroad and deductible in France, withholding on non-residents and transfer pricing documentation requirements may apply. Include beneficiary and form 2065 supplementary table if any.
